transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I suppose I’m here because I’ve been having these nights where I eat more than I mean to, and afterward I just feel awful about myself. I’ll be sitting there with crumbs and empty containers around me, and I feel so ashamed and disgusted that the next morning I can hardly pray, or even look people at church in the eye. I’m sorry, I know that sounds terrible… but I thought maybe I should talk to someone.
Can you tell me more about those times when you're eating more than you mean to? Do you feel like you can't stop or control yourself once you start?

Yes… I think that’s the part that frightens me. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but once I take that first bite, especially after the house is quiet, it’s like my good sense just sort of… steps aside.

I’ll be telling myself, “Belinda, stop now, that’s enough,” and at the same time my hands are still reaching for more. It feels like I should be able to control it, but in those moments I just don’t seem to. Is that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
During these episodes, do you feel a lack of control over how much you're eating, like you can't stop even if you want to?

Yes… yes, I do. I don’t like admitting that, because it sounds like I’m making excuses, but once I’ve started—usually when everything’s quiet—it’s like the part of me that knows better just steps aside.

I’ll be thinking, Belinda, stop now, that’s enough, and somehow my hands are still reaching for more anyway. It feels… not out of my body exactly, but like I’m not really in charge the way I ought to be. Is that what you mean?
After these eating episodes, do you ever try to make up for what you've eaten by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

I… I’m not sure how to answer that properly. I don’t think I have anything like that to tell you. I haven’t really… noticed myself doing those things, at least not in the way you mean.

Afterward I mostly just feel ashamed and upset with myself. But making myself sick or taking things… no, I don’t think so. Is that the kind of answer you needed?
Have you ever fasted, severely restricted your food, or exercised a lot more than usual after these eating episodes to make up for what you ate?

I don’t think so… not in that deliberate way. I might tell myself I’ll “be better tomorrow” or try to eat a bit less because I feel guilty, but I haven’t really fasted or done hard exercise to make up for it.

I hope that makes sense. I’m not trying to leave anything out—I just don’t think I do those things the way you’re asking.
Have you ever gone without food for an entire day or pushed yourself to exercise much harder than usual after these eating episodes to try to balance things out?

No… I don’t think I’ve gone a whole day without eating because of it. And I’m certainly not pushing myself with exercise afterward—not more than usual.

I do feel awful after, and I might make promises to myself about doing better, but not like that. I hope that answers it properly.
Do these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life in any way?

I suppose it does, yes… more than I like to admit.

I’ve started turning down some bridge nights, and even helping with the church kitchen, because I get so worried someone might notice the leftovers are missing, or ask me why I seem so embarrassed. I know that probably sounds silly, but it’s been making me avoid things I used to do. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When these episodes happen, does the eating take place in a short period of time, like within a couple of hours, or does it feel more spread out over the evening?

It’s usually more in one stretch, I think… like once I start, it can all happen in the same sitting, not just nibbling all evening.

On a bad night, I might start with a plate of leftover casserole from a funeral luncheon, and then before I quite realize it I’ve had that, and maybe half a pan of brownies, some biscuits, and whatever chicken salad is in the fridge. I’m embarrassed saying it that plainly, but yes… it’s within a couple of hours, I’d say.
Do you usually eat alone during these episodes because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

Yes… I suppose that’s true.

At bridge or church suppers I’ll take a small plate, nothing that would draw attention. Then later, after everyone’s gone home, I’ll go back into the kitchen and pull out the leftovers and eat there where no one can see me.

I’m not proud of that. It’s mostly because I’d be so embarrassed if anyone saw how much I was really eating. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking?
After these eating episodes, do you often feel guilty, depressed, or disgusted with yourself?

Yes… yes, I do.

I try not to make too much of it, because I know everybody overdoes things now and then, but after those nights I’ll sit there with crumbs and empty containers around me and just feel so ashamed. Disgusted with myself, really.

Sometimes the next morning I can hardly pray, and I don’t want to look folks at church in the eye. I worry they can somehow tell what I’ve done. Is that… is that what you mean?
